summary: The root كدح (kdH) means to work, labor, or strive diligently, often to the point of weariness, for worldly or spiritual gain.
lane: 1 كَدَحَ ذ , aor. كَدَحَ , (inf. n. كَدْحٌ , S,) He worked or wrought; laboured; employed himself actively; syn. سَعَى ; (S, K;) and عَمِلَ : (S:) he wrought for himself good or evil: (K:) he was eager, and strove, laboured, or exerted himself, and wearied himself, in work, in the affairs relating to the present world and in those relating to the world to come: (Zj:) he toiled, or laboured hard. (S, K.) هُوَ يَكْدَحُ فِى كَذَا He toils, or labours hard, in such a thing, or affair. (S.) -b2- كَدَحَ لِعِيَالِهِ , and , He sought, sought after, or sought to gain, sustenance; or he gained, acquired, or earned; for his family, or household; syn. كَسَبَ , (S, K,) or اكتسب . (L.) -A2- كَدَحَ وَجْهَهُ It (a thing, S) scratched, or lacerated, his face: (S, K:) or did to his face that which disfigured it, or rendered it ugly or unseemly: as also , (K,) inf. n. تَكْدِيحٌ : (TA:) or كدّح , inf. n. تكديح , signifies it scratched, or lacerated, much, or many times, or in many places: (S:) also [so in the L; but in the K, or] كَدَحَ in the phrase كَدَحَ وَجْهَهُ signifies أَفْسَدَ ; (K;) you say كَدَحَ وَجْهَ أَمْرِهِ , meaning he marred his affair. (L.) -b2- كَدَحَ رَأْسَهُ He separated his hair with a comb. (K.)

headwords.gloss: became scratched; lacerated, much; many times

parts.t: He fell from the flat top,

headwords.def: تكدّح It (the skin) became scratched, or lacerated, much, or many times, or in many places. (S, K.) وَقَعَ مِنَ السَّطْحِ فَتَكَدَّحَ He fell from the flat top, or roof, of the house, and became much broken [ in his skin ]. (L.)

headwords.gloss: A scratch; laceration, of the skin; i. q; more

parts.t: laceration, of the skin; i. q.
He has upon him a scratch, &c.

headwords.def: كَدْحٌ A scratch, or laceration, of the skin; i. q. خَدْشٌ : (S, K:) or a كَدْح is more (or larger, L) than a خَدْش : (S:) any mark made by scratching or biting: (IAth:) pl. كُدُوحٌ . (S, K.) Ex. بِهِ كَدْحٌ , (S, K,) and كُدُوحٌ , (S,) He has upon him a scratch, &c. (S, K.)

headwords.gloss: Verily thou workest; labourest; workest for thyself good
headwords.def: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَى رَبِّكَ , [Kur lxxxiv. 6,] Verily thou workest, or labourest, (S,) or, workest for thyself good or evil, (TA,) or, strivest, or labourest, in thy work until the meeting of thy Lord, i. e., until death. (Jel.)

headwords.gloss: An ass much lacerated by the bites of other asses

parts.t: An ass much lacerated by the bites of other asses.
(S, K.) A wild ass is termed
because he is lacerated by the bites of other asses. (A'Obeyd.)

headwords.def: حِمَارٌ مُكَدَّحٌ An ass much lacerated by the bites of other asses. (S, K.) A wild ass is termed مكدّح because he is lacerated by the bites of other asses. (A'Obeyd.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
